'''Marcus Smart''' (born March 6, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]].  He is considered a top prospect for the [[2014 NBA Draft]], having declared on April 7, 2014.

==Early years==
Smart is the son of Camellia Smart and Billy Frank Smart. He has three older brothers, Todd Westbrook (deceased), Jeff Westbrook and Michael Smart.<ref>{{cite web|title=Smart went from 'dead or in jail' to Oklahoma State's selfless general|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/big12/2013/01/22/mens-college-basketball-oklahoma-state-marcus-smart-profile/1850729/|work=USA TODAY|last=Prisbell|first=Eric|accessdate=January 22, 2013|date=January 22, 2013}}</ref> He attended [[Edward S. Marcus High School]] in [[Flower Mound, Texas]], along with one of his current OSU teammates, Phillip Forte. During his senior year, Smart averaged 15.1 points, 9.2 rebounds and 5 assists.<ref name=2011-12ESPNHS>{{cite web|title=2011-12 ESPNHS All-Americans|url=http://espn.go.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/7811369/2011-12-espnhs-boys-basketball-all-americans|work=ESPN|last=Flores|first=Ronnie|last2=Huff|first2=Doug|accessdate=April 11, 2014|date=April 17, 2012}}</ref> In his high school career, he achieved a record of 115–6 through 3 seasons and was a 2-time State 5A champion. He was also named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and was an ESPNHS first team All-American.<ref name=2011-12ESPNHS/> Marcus played competitive football until the sixth grade and enjoys playing tennis in his spare time.<ref>[http://www.okstate.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/smart_marcus00.html]</ref>

==College career==
During his freshman year at [[Oklahoma State]], Smart led the Cowboys to a 24–8 record and finished 3rd place in the Big 12 behind [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]. Smart averaged 15.4 PPG, 5.8 RPG, and 4.2 APG and led the Big 12 in steals where he recorded 99 and averaged 3.0 per game. Smart and the Cowboys earned a trip to the NCAA bracket that year clinching a #5 seed in the Midwest Region. During the first round of the tournament though, the Cowboys were eliminated by the #12 seed [[Oregon Ducks]]. On April 17, 2013, Smart held a press conference in the student union at OSU and announced that he would not declare for the NBA draft and instead, return to OSU for his sophomore season. During that same press conference, [[Le'Bryan Nash]] and Markel Brown also announced that they would return to OSU for the 2013–14 season. On November 19, 2013 Smart tied an OSU single game scoring record with 39 points leading his #7 Oklahoma State Cowboys past #11 [[Memphis Tigers]].

He was considered one of the top prospects for the [[2013 NBA Draft]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Marcus-Smart-6284/|title=DraftExpress NBA Draft Prospect Profile: Marcus Smart, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook|accessdate=January 6, 2013}}</ref> though on April 16 it was reported by Sports Illustrated that he had decided to stay at Oklahoma State and return for his sophomore season in 2013–14.<ref>[http://tracking.si.com/2013/04/16/okla-state-marcus-smart-returning-to-school/ Report: Okla. State’s Marcus Smart to return for sophomore year | SI Tracking Blog – Tracking MLB, NBA, NFL, NHL, and NCAA On Twitter]</ref>

On February 8, 2014, at a game at [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], Smart shoved a fan in the stands after a verbal altercation in the closing minutes of the game, and received a technical foul following it. It had been previously reported that Smart told his coaches that the fan used a racial slur after Smart crashed into the stands.  At a press conference the following afternoon, neither Smart nor coach [[Travis Ford]] addressed the question of what the fan said, and OSU announced that Smart would be suspended for 3 games because of the incident.<ref>Brendan Malloy, [http://tracking.si.com/2014/02/09/marcus-smart-suspended-3-games/ "Marcus Smart suspended 3 games for altercation with fan"], ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', February 9, 2014.</ref> Separately, Texas Tech announced its finding that the fan had not used a racial slur but had spoken inappropriately to Smart, and that the fan had agreed not to attend any further Texas Tech games during the 2013-2014 season.<ref>[http://www.texastech.com/genrel/020914aab.html "Statement Regarding Incident At Texas Tech-Oklahoma State Men's Basketball Game"], [[Texas Tech University]], February 9, 2014.</ref> On February 13, he was named one of the 30 finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2013-14 Men's Naismith Trophy Midseason 30|url=http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx|work=Naismith Awards|accessdate=February 14, 2014|date=February 13, 2014}}</ref> In the first game of the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]], the Cowboys lost to [[Gonzaga]]. He finished with 23 points, 13 rebounds, 7 assists and 6 steals, becoming the first player in tournament history to record 20 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists and 5 steals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart can’t get first NCAA tournament win as his Cowboys fall to Gonzaga|url=http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/03/21/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-lose-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament/|work=Sports Illustrated|last=Mandel|first=Stewart|accessdate=March 21, 2014|date=March 21, 2014}}</ref>

==NBA career==
On April 7, 2014, Smart announced his intention to enter the 2014 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart entering NBA draft|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10746052/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-cowboys-entering-nba-draft|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 7, 2014|date=April 7, 2014}}</ref>
